body.statement: The mechanisms in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) are strictly positive and rational and induce \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\), whose latent projections are \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\) and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i\), with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\})\), \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M}\), and \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}\). Both models therefore belong to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}})\). Moreover \(P_{\sigma}(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)=r_a\) and \(P_{\sigma}(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)=1/2\), while \(P(C_i=d,S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)=3/16\) for every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\). Hence \(P_{\sigma}(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)=3/64\), \(P_{\sigma}(S_i=1)=3/8\), and the two full selected observational laws assign probability \(1/8\) to every observed cell. Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), \(P_+(Y_i=1)=9/16\), \(P_-(Y_i=1)=7/16\), and both selection normalizers equal \(3/8\). At the root role state, \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1;0)=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1;0)=1/2\), whereas \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)=9/32\) and \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)=7/32\), so the conditional effects are \(9/16\) and \(7/16\). The connected \(C_i\) is informative before selection because \(P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=3/4\neq1/4=P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0)\). The pair \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) consists of nested \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\)-rooted C-forests, with \(V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\}\), \(V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing\), and \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}(\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\})\); \(D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing\), so they form the terminal selected hedge for \((\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\},\{X_i\})\). Finally, replacing only \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) by \(1/2\) preserves the graph and equality of the two selected observational laws but yields denominators \(25/41\) and \(23/39\); therefore the displayed denominator equality is a tuned informative cancellation, not a structural consequence of the graph.
body.justification: The explicit table proves that denominator locking can survive genuinely informative conditioning and selection without being imposed by graph separation or isolation.
body.gap: Existing selected hedges separate interventional kernels but do not exhibit a connected conditioning coordinate with exact full-law equality, a positive equal denominator, an unequal numerator, and a same-graph nonlocking perturbation.
body.consumer: The example is a mandatory positive-control certificate for implementations of rational selected-hedge synthesis and verification.
body.proof_tex:
All variables in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) are binary.  The displayed local success probabilities and their complements belong to
\[
 \left\{\frac14,\frac12,\frac34,
              \frac5{16},\frac7{16},\frac9{16},\frac{11}{16}\right\},
\]
so every local entry is rational and strictly between zero and one.  The table for \(X_i\) changes with \(U_i\); the table for \(Y_i\) changes with each of \(X_i\) and \(U_i\); the table for \(C_i\) changes with \(Y_i\); and the table for \(S_i\) changes with each of \(Y_i\) and \(C_i\).  Thus the parent relations are exactly those of \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\).

Marginalizing \(U_i\) produces the directed edge \(X_i\to Y_i\) and the bidirected edge \(X_i\leftrightarrow Y_i\) induced by \(X_i\leftarrow U_i\to Y_i\); the other displayed arrows have no latent internal vertex and remain.  No further latent-projection edge is created because every other path has an observed internal vertex.  This is precisely \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\).  In the selected projection onto \(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}\), all three observed vertices are ancestors of \(S_i\), so the adjacent endpoint marks are tails.  The pairs \((X_i,Y_i)\) and \((Y_i,C_i)\) are adjacent, whereas \(X_i\) and \(C_i\) are separated by \(\{Y_i\}\) conditional on \(S_i\): in the ancestral moral graph for \(\{X_i,C_i,Y_i,S_i\}\), removing the conditioned vertices \(Y_i,S_i\) leaves \(C_i\) disconnected from the component containing \(X_i\).  Hence the observed MAG is exactly the undirected noncollider chain
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i.
\]
The three-node noncollider equivalence class has no invariant endpoint mark, so its input-free completed partial graph is \(X_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}Y_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}C_i=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\).  This proves
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}),
 \quad \mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M},
 \quad \mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}.
\]
Together with positivity, rationality, and binary support, \(\text{def:rational-binary-class}\) gives
\(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+},\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}
\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}})\).

We now calculate the laws.  Since \(P(U_i=1)=1/2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(X_i=1)&=\tfrac12\tfrac14+\tfrac12\tfrac34=\tfrac12,&
 P(U_i=1\mid X_i=1)&=\frac{(1/2)(3/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac34=r_1,\\
 P(X_i=0)&=\tfrac12\tfrac34+\tfrac12\tfrac14=\tfrac12,&
 P(U_i=1\mid X_i=0)&=\frac{(1/2)(1/4)}{1/2}=\tfrac14=r_0.
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{9}
\]
Thus, for \(a\in\{0,1\}\), iterated expectation and the outcome table give
\[
 P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)
 =\frac12+\frac{\sigma}{4}
   \{P(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)-r_a\}=\frac12.                \tag{10}
\]
For every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\), multiplication of the \(C_i\) and \(S_i\) tables yields
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
 (b,d)&(0,0)&(0,1)&(1,0)&(1,1)\\ \hline
 P(C_i=d,S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)
 &(3/4)(1/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(1/4)(3/4)&(3/4)(1/4)
\end{array}
=\frac3{16}.                                             \tag{11}
\]
Combining \(P(X_i=a)=1/2\), (10), and (11),
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac3{16}=\frac3{64}.       \tag{12}
\]
Summing (12) over the eight observed cells gives \(P_\sigma(S_i=1)=3/8\), and division gives
\[
 P_\sigma(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d\mid S_i=1)
 =\frac{3/64}{3/8}=\frac18.                              \tag{13}
\]
The selected observational laws are therefore identical and have full support.

Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), the intervention deletes the \(U_i\to X_i\) factor but leaves \(U_i\) fair.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_+(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12+\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac9{16},\\
 P_-(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=\frac12-\frac14\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)=\frac7{16}.       \tag{14}
\end{aligned}
\]
Equation (11) gives \(P(C_i=d,S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)=3/16\) and therefore
\[
 P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)=\sum_{d=0}^1\frac3{16}=\frac38.     \tag{15}
\]
It follows from (14)--(15) that each interventional selection normalizer is \(3/8\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},\sigma}}(1;0)
 &=\frac{\sum_b P_\sigma(Y_i=b\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))(3/16)}{3/8}
 =\frac12,                                                \tag{16}\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac{(9/16)(3/16)}{3/8}=\frac9{32},                  \tag{17}\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)
 &=\frac{(7/16)(3/16)}{3/8}=\frac7{32}.                  \tag{18}
\end{aligned}
\]
The positive common denominator in (16) turns (17)--(18) into conditional effects \(9/16\) and \(7/16\).  Also, directly from the \(C_i\) table,
\[
 P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=\frac34\ne\frac14=P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0),
\]
so the conditioning coordinate is genuinely informative before selection.

For the graphical obstruction, \(F_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is bidirected-connected, every vertex has at most one directed child, and its unique childless root is \(Y_i\).  The singleton \(F'_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is a proper C-subforest with the same root.  Directly,
\[
 V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\},\qquad
 V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing.
\]
After intervening on \(X_i\), the root \(Y_i\) is still an ancestor of the terminal set \(\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\}\), indeed it is a member of that set and has directed paths to \(C_i\) and \(S_i\).  Thus
\[
 R_{\mathrm{inf}}=\{Y_i\}
 \subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}
 (\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\}).                                     \tag{19}
\]
There is no intervention-input vertex, so the maximal selection-exchange coordinate for this terminal query is \(D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing\).  The bidirected connectivity, common-root, treatment-intersection, ancestry, and empty-exchange checks above are exactly the terminal selected-hedge predicates in \(\text{def:informative-graph-certificate}\).  Hence \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) is the asserted terminal selected hedge.

Finally modify only the cell \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) from \(1/4\) to \(1/2\).  The changed selection table remains strictly positive and still depends on both parents.  Equations (9)--(10) are unchanged, so both signs have the same unselected observed law; the common modified \(C_i,S_i\) mechanisms then imply the same full selected observational law for both signs.  If
\(p=P_\sigma(Y_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))\), the modified table gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac38+p\frac9{16}=\frac{6+3p}{16},\\
 P(C_i=1,S_i=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_i=0))
 &=(1-p)\frac3{16}+p\frac38=\frac{3+3p}{16}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently the modified denominator is
\[
 \widetilde D_\sigma=\frac{1+p}{2+p}.
\]
Substitution of \(p=9/16\) and \(p=7/16\) from (14) yields
\[
 \widetilde D_+=\frac{25}{41},\qquad
 \widetilde D_-=\frac{23}{39},
\]
which are unequal.  The original equality (16) is therefore an exact cancellation of the informative mechanisms, not a consequence of the represented graph.
